statement: Fixed after counting the calibration third and BEFORE counting the held-out two thirds. The held-out result is reported whichever way it lands.
question: Can the real token cost of a rendered text image be predicted from its pixel size alone — and does that, with the text token count, pick the cheaper encoding? Is chars-per-text-token (v1's framing) enough on its own?

law.form: real image tokens = a × ceil(width × height / 750) + b, least squares on the 32 calibration samples

thumb.form: image is cheaper when characters per text token < c*, for full lines of this renderer

rules.rule: the law predicts each held-out image's real token count: median absolute error ≤ 3% and worst ≤ 10%
the law plus the text token count picks the cheaper encoding on ≥ 90% of held-out samples (a tie counts either way)
chars-per-text-token alone (the one-number rule) picks correctly on < 75% of held-out samples — image cost follows rendered area, and short lines waste it
every held-out hex and base64 sample (16) is cheaper as an image
every held-out law, code and key=value sample (24) is cheaper as text

alsoReported: prose, JSON and CSV per sample — the calibration third put them near break-even, so no direction is predicted
